title: The Chinese Towns Where the Streets Are Water | China Travel Expert
description:
In these Chinese towns, the streets are made of water — and for centuries, a boat was the only way to your front door.

The water towns of Jiangnan (around Shanghai, Suzhou and Hangzhou) are laced with canals instead of roads, lined with whitewashed walls and black-tiled roofs and stitched together by old stone bridges. They grew rich in the Ming and Qing dynasties, when grain barges moved along these very canals. Zhouzhuang — founded almost a thousand years ago in the Northern Song — has a network of waterways crossed by fourteen stone bridges, which is why it's nicknamed the "Venice of the East."

🧭 Expert Tip: Arrive at dawn. The canals go glassy and quiet before the day-tour boats and crowds arrive — the same town feels completely different by 10am.

在这些中国古镇，街道是水做的——一条小船，曾是回家的唯一路。
